summary: This study describes a radical-enhanced atomic layer deposition (REALD) process for growing tungsten oxide (WO3-x) films with tunable oxygen vacancy (VO) concentrations. The process uses WH2(Cp)2 as the W-precursor and O* and H* radicals as reactants. The VO concentration can be controlled by adjusting the O* and H* exposure times, with the highest VO concentration achieved at 5 at.%. The films exhibit good uniformity and can be used for electronic applications such as resistive random-access memory (ReRAM).
